diagrams.visual_summary: The schematic illustrates a multi-scale Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) backbone paired with a Feature Pyramid Network (FPN). On the left, a 3x3 sliding convolution kernel extracts spatial features. The middle column contrasts a Deep Stride-32 semantic feature map (low spatial resolution, high semantic context) with a Shallow Stride-8 high-resolution layer (fine edge localization). A 1x1 Lateral Connection Bridge aligns channel dimensions and merges top-down upsampled semantic features with bottom-up spatial features to feed Multi-Scale FPN Output Heads (P3, P4, P5).

components.lab_question: LAB CALIBRATION C0-A: Click or drag a bounding box around the 3x3 Convolution Filter Kernel scanning the input image.
components.socratic_hint: Look at the leftmost block showing the 3x3 sliding weight matrix scanning over the input grid.
components.explanation: The 3x3 Convolution Kernel shares weights across all (H, W) spatial positions, providing translation equivariance with minimal parameter overhead.

components.lab_question: LAB CALIBRATION C0-B: Point to the 1x1 Lateral Connection Bridge that aligns channels and fuses top-down and shallow feature maps.
components.socratic_hint: Check the green connector between the middle backbone layers and the right-hand FPN output heads.
components.explanation: 1x1 lateral connections align channel depth between shallow high-resolution feature maps and upsampled deep semantic layers prior to element-wise addition.

vqa_challenge.question: Why does the Feature Pyramid Network fuse the Deep Stride-32 layer with the Shallow Stride-8 layer?
vqa_challenge.reference_answer: The 1x1 lateral connection fuses deep high-level semantic features with shallow high-resolution spatial features to detect objects across multiple scales.
vqa_challenge.sample_correct_answer: It merges deep semantic context from Stride-32 with sharp spatial detail from Stride-8 so multi-scale heads detect both small and large objects.
vqa_challenge.sample_partial_answer: It connects deep and shallow layers so the detector handles different object sizes.
vqa_challenge.misconception_trap_answer: The 1x1 lateral connection never fuses deep semantic features with shallow spatial layers, which prevents detecting objects across multiple scales.

diagrams.visual_summary: The diagram is divided into two conceptual stages: Intersection over Union (IoU) geometry on the left and Non-Maximum Suppression (NMS) filtering on the right. On the left, two bounding boxes A and B intersect over a highlighted green Intersection Overlap Area (A n B), normalized by their total union area (A u B). In the center, a cluster of Duplicate Overlapping Ghost Boxes surrounds the same target object, which NMS filters into a single Surviving NMS Best Bounding Box (confidence 0.96) on the far right.

components.lab_question: LAB CALIBRATION C1-A: Click or box the green Intersection Overlap Area (A n B) that forms the numerator of the IoU metric.
components.socratic_hint: Look at the shared overlapping region inside the two intersecting rectangles on the left side of the schematic.
components.explanation: Intersection over Union (IoU) divides the shared intersection area (A n B) by the combined union area (A u B) to produce a scale-invariant overlap score in [0, 1].

components.lab_question: LAB CALIBRATION C1-B: Point to the Surviving NMS Best Bounding Box (Score 0.96) after duplicate ghost detections are suppressed.
components.socratic_hint: Inspect the rightmost panel showing the clean final detection that remains after duplicate suppression.
components.explanation: Non-Maximum Suppression (NMS) sorts candidate boxes by confidence score, retains the highest-scoring box (0.96), and removes overlapping neighbors whose IoU exceeds the threshold.

vqa_challenge.question: How does Non-Maximum Suppression (NMS) filter duplicate overlapping bounding boxes around an object?
vqa_challenge.reference_answer: NMS keeps the highest-confidence bounding box and suppresses lower-scoring neighboring boxes whose IoU overlap exceeds a threshold.
vqa_challenge.sample_correct_answer: It retains the box with the highest confidence score and removes redundant overlapping boxes that have high IoU with it.
vqa_challenge.sample_partial_answer: It picks the best box and deletes extra boxes nearby.
vqa_challenge.misconception_trap_answer: NMS never keeps the highest-confidence bounding box, which duplicates lower-scoring neighboring boxes when IoU overlap is low.

diagrams.visual_summary: The diagram depicts the single-stage YOLO object detection pipeline in three horizontal stages. On the left, the input image is partitioned into an S x S Spatial Grid where the cell containing the object's center (cx, cy) is assigned prediction ownership. In the middle, the CSPDarknet Backbone & PANet Neck extract and aggregate multi-scale features in a single forward pass. On the right, a Decoupled Detection Head splits into parallel convolutional branches for bounding-box coordinate regression (CIoU loss) and class probability prediction (BCE loss).

components.target_label: S x S Spatial Grid & Target Center Cell
components.dino_prompt: yellow S x S spatial grid box.
components.lab_question: LAB CALIBRATION C2-A: Click or box the S x S Spatial Grid where the cell containing the object's center (cx, cy) predicts the bounding box.
components.socratic_hint: Focus on the leftmost stage displaying the grid overlay and the highlighted target center cell.
components.explanation: YOLO divides the input frame into an S x S grid and assigns object detection responsibility strictly to the grid cell containing the object's center (cx, cy).

components.lab_question: LAB CALIBRATION C2-B: Point to the Decoupled Detection Head that separates bounding-box coordinate regression from class probability prediction.
components.socratic_hint: Look at the rightmost purple block where the output splits into separate Box and Class branches.
components.explanation: A decoupled detection head separates spatial coordinate regression (x, y, w, h) from semantic class probability prediction, speeding convergence and boosting AP.

vqa_challenge.question: Why does the YOLO detector use a decoupled detection head at the end of the network?
vqa_challenge.reference_answer: The decoupled detection head separates bounding-box coordinate regression from class probability prediction into independent branches to prevent task conflict.
vqa_challenge.sample_correct_answer: It splits spatial bounding-box regression and class probability prediction into separate branches so localization and classification do not interfere.
vqa_challenge.sample_partial_answer: It uses two branches to predict the box location and the object class.
vqa_challenge.misconception_trap_answer: The decoupled detection head never separates bounding-box regression from class prediction, which causes task conflict across branches.

diagrams.concept_title: OCR: Scene Text Detection, CRNN & CTC Loss
diagrams.visual_summary: The diagram shows a Convolutional Recurrent Neural Network (CRNN) optical character recognition pipeline from left to right. First, CNN Vertical Feature Slices convert a cropped word image into a left-to-right sequence of vertical column feature vectors (t1..tT). Second, a Bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM) Sequence Encoder propagates sequential context both forward and backward across the slices. Third, a CTC Blank-Token Collapse Decoder merges duplicate adjacent character emissions and removes blank tokens (_) to produce the final variable-length word without character-level bounding boxes.

components.lab_question: LAB CALIBRATION C3-A: Click or box the Bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM) Sequence Encoder that models left-to-right and right-to-left context.
components.socratic_hint: Select the central purple module located between the CNN feature slices and the CTC decoder.
components.explanation: The Bidirectional LSTM processes vertical feature columns in both directions, capturing sequential character context to disambiguate similar glyphs.

components.lab_question: LAB CALIBRATION C3-B: Point to the CTC Blank-Token Collapse Decoder that merges repeated consecutive characters and strips blank tokens.
components.socratic_hint: Look at the green decoder block on the right side of the CRNN diagram.
components.explanation: Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC) collapses consecutive identical character predictions and strips blank tokens (_) to align variable-length text transcripts.

vqa_challenge.question: How does the CTC decoder in CRNN convert frame-level character predictions into a final word?
vqa_challenge.reference_answer: The CTC decoder collapses consecutive duplicate character emissions and removes blank tokens to form the final recognized word.
vqa_challenge.sample_correct_answer: It merges repeated adjacent character predictions into a single letter and strips out the blank separator tokens.
vqa_challenge.sample_partial_answer: It removes extra repeated letters and blanks to output the word.
vqa_challenge.misconception_trap_answer: The CTC decoder never collapses duplicate character emissions and keeps blank tokens to prevent forming the recognized word.

diagrams.concept_title: End-to-End Vision Pipelines: Combining YOLO + OCR
diagrams.visual_summary: The schematic depicts a two-stage cascaded scene-text recognition pipeline. On the left, Stage 1: Real-Time YOLO Detector localizes text regions in the full camera frame and filters duplicates with NMS. In the middle, the ROI Crop & Perspective Rectification Stage extracts each detected bounding box, deskews tilted perspective geometry, and normalizes height (H=32) while preserving aspect ratio. On the right, Stage 2: CRNN + CTC OCR Reader decodes the rectified crop into characters and computes the joint end-to-end confidence score (P_YOLO x P_OCR).

components.dino_prompt: blue ROI crop and rectify box.
components.lab_question: LAB CALIBRATION C4-A: Click or box the ROI Crop & Perspective Rectification module that deskews tilted text between YOLO and OCR.
components.socratic_hint: Click the blue intermediate module connecting Stage 1 (YOLO Detector) and Stage 2 (CRNN OCR Reader).
components.explanation: The ROI Crop & Perspective Rectification stage deskews rotated text boxes and normalizes image height while preserving aspect ratio before feeding the CRNN sequence reader.

components.dino_prompt: green stage 2 CRNN CTC OCR box.
components.lab_question: LAB CALIBRATION C4-B: Point to Stage 2: CRNN + CTC OCR Reader, which decodes the character sequence and multiplies YOLO x OCR confidence.
components.socratic_hint: Select the rightmost green stage that performs CRNN sequence decoding on the rectified crop.
components.explanation: Running Stage 2 (CRNN + CTC OCR) exclusively on rectified YOLO crops avoids scanning 98% background clutter and combines detection and recognition confidence.

vqa_challenge.question: What is the role of the ROI Crop and Perspective Rectification stage between YOLO and CRNN OCR?
vqa_challenge.reference_answer: ROI rectification crops the detected text region and deskews perspective tilt into a normalized horizontal strip for the CRNN sequence reader.
vqa_challenge.sample_correct_answer: It isolates the bounding box found by YOLO and straightens tilted text into a flat horizontal strip before OCR sequence decoding.
vqa_challenge.sample_partial_answer: It crops out the text box and straightens it for the OCR model.
vqa_challenge.misconception_trap_answer: ROI rectification never crops the detected text region, which increases perspective tilt and prevents CRNN sequence decoding.
